stem: A company publishes an Azure web app and wants managed rules that catch common OWASP web attacks. Which service is the fundamentals fit?

choices.text: Microsoft Entra access reviews
Privileged Identity Management
Azure Web Application Firewall associated with the published web front end
Microsoft Purview records management

explanation: WAF managed rules protect published web applications from common HTTP attacks. Access reviews, PIM, and records management do not inspect web requests.

stem: An Azure subscription already has posture recommendations. Security also wants Microsoft 365 email, device, and identity incidents in one XDR queue. Why is Defender for Cloud not that XDR queue?

choices.text: Defender for Cloud is the Microsoft Defender portal incident queue
Defender for Cloud replaces Defender for Office 365 Safe Links
Defender for Cloud is Microsoft Entra ID
Defender for Cloud is cloud-security posture and workload protection; Microsoft Defender XDR unifies Microsoft 365 Defender workload incidents

explanation: Defender for Cloud is Azure/multicloud posture and workload protection. The Microsoft 365 Defender XDR family and Defender portal incident queue are a different control plane.

stem: CSPM reports a SQL database with public exposure. Separately, EDR shows a malicious process on a VM. Which statement keeps those findings in the right capability class?

choices.text: The public-exposure finding is posture/misconfiguration; the malicious process is runtime threat detection
Both findings are Privileged Identity Management activations
Both findings are retention-label events
CSPM is the only Microsoft EDR sensor

explanation: Public exposure is a CSPM posture issue. A malicious process is runtime detection such as workload protection or EDR. Mixing those classes hides the right control.

subobjective: Describe enhanced security features provided by cloud workload protection
stem: A Linux server in Azure needs Defender for Cloud workload protection. A user laptop needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: They are the same SKU and the same portal queue
Defender for Servers is a cloud workload protection plan; Defender for Endpoint is the Microsoft 365 device EDR workload
Defender for Endpoint is only for Azure SQL databases
Defender for Servers replaces Microsoft Entra ID Protection

explanation: Cloud workload protection plans such as Defender for Servers protect cloud/server workloads in Defender for Cloud. Defender for Endpoint is the Microsoft 365 XDR device workload. Learners should not collapse them into one product.

source.title: Plan a Defender for Servers deployment - Microsoft Defender for Cloud

subobjective: Describe how security policies, standards, and recommendations improve the cloud security posture
stem: Assigning a security standard in Defender for Cloud created recommendations. A learner says those recommendations are Microsoft Purview improvement actions. What is wrong?

choices.text: Purview improvement actions are the only way to encrypt Azure disks
Defender for Cloud recommendations recertify Entra guest groups
Defender for Cloud recommendations close Azure/multicloud posture gaps; Compliance Manager improvement actions track customer compliance controls
They are the same because both are Azure Bastion logs

explanation: Standards-driven recommendations in Defender for Cloud are cloud-posture work. Compliance Manager improvement actions are a Purview compliance-management concept.

subobjective: Define the concepts of security information and event management (SIEM) and security orchestration automated response (SOAR)
stem: A SOC deploys Microsoft Sentinel and correlates alerts well but still handles every response by hand. Which gap is that?

choices.text: Sentinel cannot be a SIEM unless Azure Bastion is enabled
Manual response means hashing has replaced SOAR
The SOC must switch to records management to automate containment
SIEM detection without SOAR automation leaves repeatable response steps manual

explanation: A SIEM can detect and investigate without automatically responding. SOAR/playbooks are what automate repeatable response. Detection alone is not full SOAR.

subobjective: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel
stem: A company wants one SIEM to ingest Microsoft 365, Azure, and third-party firewall logs. Why is Microsoft Defender XDR not a complete substitute?

choices.text: Defender XDR correlates Microsoft workload signals; Sentinel is the cloud SIEM that is designed to ingest a broad set of sources including non-Microsoft logs
Defender XDR is the only Microsoft service that can store firewall syslog
Sentinel cannot ingest Microsoft 365 logs
Third-party firewall logs can be ingested only by Azure Bastion

explanation: XDR is optimized around Microsoft Defender workloads. Sentinel is the SIEM that can connect many data sources, including non-Microsoft logs.

source.title: What is Microsoft Sentinel SIEM?

subobjective: Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel
stem: Leadership asks whether Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR are the same product. Which distinction is accurate?

choices.text: Defender XDR is the only Microsoft SIEM, and Sentinel is only a WAF
Sentinel is a cloud SIEM/SOAR that can ingest many sources; Defender XDR correlates Microsoft workload signals into a unified incident view
Sentinel replaces Entra ID, and Defender XDR replaces Azure virtual networks
They are identical names for Compliance Manager

explanation: Sentinel is SIEM/SOAR across diverse logs. Defender XDR natively correlates Microsoft 365 Defender workloads. They integrate but are not the same control.

stem: Which service is not a Microsoft Defender XDR workload in current SC-900 training?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
Azure Firewall
Microsoft Defender for Identity

explanation: Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, and Identity are XDR workloads. Azure Firewall is an Azure network control, not a Defender XDR workload.

stem: Safe Attachments detonates email files in a sandbox. Safe Links checks URLs when users click them. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Safe Links replaces Safe Attachments, so file detonation is never needed
Both features are Azure Firewall DNAT rules
Safe Attachments is a Conditional Access named location
They are complementary Defender for Office 365 controls for files versus URLs

explanation: Safe Attachments and Safe Links address different email/collaboration objects: files and URLs. Current SC-900 training treats both as Defender for Office 365 capabilities.

source.title: Why do I need Microsoft Defender for Office 365? - Microsoft Defender for Office 365

stem: A workstation needs behavioral blocking and forensic investigation of a running process. A domain controller needs detections for ticket theft. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Defender for Endpoint for the workstation EDR; Defender for Identity for Active Directory identity attacks
Defender for Identity is the laptop EDR agent
Defender for Endpoint analyzes Kerberos ticket attacks on domain controllers as its primary job
Both needs are met only by Azure WAF

explanation: Endpoint EDR and Active Directory identity threat detection are different Defender workloads. Mixing them is a common SC-900 error.

source.title: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

subobjective: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
stem: Unsanctioned SaaS discovery is in scope. Phishing in Exchange Online is in scope. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Defender for Office 365 is the CASB that inventories unsanctioned SaaS
Defender for Cloud Apps for the CASB/SaaS problem; Defender for Office 365 for email and collaboration threats
Defender for Cloud Apps detonates mailbox attachments as Safe Attachments
Both problems are solved only by Azure Key Vault

explanation: CASB and email protection are different Defender workloads. Cloud Apps is not Safe Attachments, and Defender for Office 365 is not the shadow-IT inventory.

stem: A learner says Microsoft Defender for Identity is the tool that synchronizes on-premises users into Entra ID. What is the accurate correction?

choices.text: Defender for Identity is the only supported hybrid sync engine
Entra Connect is an XDR email workload
Hybrid identity sync is Entra Connect (or related sync); Defender for Identity detects identity attacks in Active Directory
Pass-the-ticket detections require password hash synchronization to be disabled

explanation: Entra Connect (and related hybrid identity tooling) synchronizes identities. Defender for Identity is a threat-detection workload for Active Directory, not the sync engine.

source.title: Microsoft Defender for Identity Overview - Microsoft Defender for Identity

stem: A device has an unpatched browser CVE. A mailbox has a malware attachment. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Vulnerability Management detonates mailbox attachments
Safe Attachments closes CVEs on endpoints
Both needs are met only by Azure DDoS Protection
Defender Vulnerability Management ranks the software weakness; Defender for Office 365 handles the email malware

explanation: Vulnerability management is exposure and weakness prioritization. Email malware is Defender for Office 365. They are not interchangeable.

source.title: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management - Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management

subobjective: Describe Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence (Defender TI)
stem: An analyst has a suspicious domain and wants actor, infrastructure, and intel-article context from Microsoft. How does Defender Threat Intelligence differ from Sentinel hunting?

choices.text: Defender TI provides threat-actor and infrastructure intelligence; Sentinel hunting queries the organization's own log data
Sentinel hunting is Microsoft's public actor encyclopedia, and Defender TI is only NSG logging
Defender TI recertifies guest users
They are both sensitivity-label templates

explanation: Defender TI is threat-intelligence context. Sentinel hunting searches collected tenant telemetry. They are complementary, not interchangeable.

source.title: Microsoft Threat Intelligence in Microsoft Defender XDR - Microsoft Defender XDR

stem: SOC analysts want one console for Defender XDR incidents. Compliance analysts want Purview solutions. Cloud operators want Azure resource security. Which mapping is accurate?

choices.text: The Defender portal is the only place to declare records and manage Azure VMs
Microsoft Defender portal for XDR operations, Purview portal for compliance, Azure portal for Azure resource security
The Purview portal investigates endpoint process trees
The Azure portal is Microsoft's only eDiscovery console

explanation: Those portals align to different jobs: XDR operations, compliance/data governance, and Azure resource management. They should not be treated as one interchangeable console.

source.title: Microsoft Defender XDR in the Microsoft Defender portal - Microsoft Defender XDR

stem: A manager says CSPM will detect a running malware process on a VM the same way EDR does. What is the accurate correction?

choices.text: CSPM is Microsoft's EDR agent and replaces Defender for Endpoint
CSPM is only a retention label
CSPM assesses configuration posture; detecting running threats on a workload is cloud workload protection or endpoint detection
CSPM issues FIDO2 keys to virtual machines

explanation: CSPM is misconfiguration and standards posture. Runtime threat detection belongs to workload protection or EDR, not to CSPM alone.

subobjective: Define the concepts of security information and event management (SIEM) and security orchestration automated response (SOAR)
stem: In Microsoft Sentinel, analytics rules raise incidents from correlated data, while playbooks then run automated actions. Which mapping is accurate?

choices.text: Playbooks correlate logs, and analytics rules physically isolate racks
Both features are sensitivity labels
Analytics rules are Azure Bastion sessions
Analytics rules are SIEM detection; playbooks are SOAR automation

explanation: Sentinel uses analytics for detection (SIEM) and playbooks for automated response (SOAR). Learners should not reverse those jobs.

source.title: Describe the Capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel

stem: Defender XDR can automatically disrupt an in-progress attack across workloads. How should a learner contrast that with a SIEM that still needs an analyst to run a playbook?

choices.text: XDR can take coordinated Microsoft-workload actions; a SIEM still depends on ingested data plus detection and (often) orchestrated response you configure
A SIEM always automatically disables Entra users with no configuration, and XDR cannot contain anything
XDR is only a WAF, and a SIEM is only a retention label
They are the same because both are Azure Key Vault

explanation: Defender XDR is built around Microsoft workload correlation and automated disruption. A SIEM such as Sentinel is broader log correlation plus SOAR you design. Neither is WAF, retention, or Key Vault.

stem: A campaign delivers malware inside email attachments. Why is Defender for Office 365 a better primary control than Azure WAF for that scenario?

choices.text: WAF is Microsoft's Safe Attachments engine
Defender for Office 365 inspects email and collaboration content; WAF inspects HTTP web-app traffic
Defender for Office 365 only protects Azure public IPs
Email attachments are filtered only by network security groups

explanation: Email malware and phishing are Defender for Office 365. WAF protects web applications. NSGs do not detonate mailbox attachments.

stem: An EDR investigation can isolate a compromised laptop from the network while the incident is handled. Which workload provides that device-response action class?

choices.text: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Azure Web Application Firewall
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Service Trust Portal

explanation: Device isolation and related EDR response actions belong to Defender for Endpoint. Compliance Manager, WAF, and STP do not isolate endpoints.

stem: Conditional Access can require a compliant device. Defender for Cloud Apps can also monitor or control a session after the user is in a SaaS app. What is the CASB adding?

choices.text: Replacement of Entra ID as the identity provider
Replacement of Azure Key Vault for certificate issuance
Replacement of Defender for Endpoint sensors
App and session visibility or control inside cloud apps, beyond the initial access decision

explanation: The CASB adds SaaS app discovery and in-app/session controls. It does not replace Entra ID, Key Vault, or endpoint sensors.

stem: The identity team wants detections for reconnaissance and lateral movement that start in on-premises Active Directory. Where do Defender for Identity sensors typically get those signals?

choices.text: From Active Directory environment signals, commonly via sensors aligned to domain controllers or AD FS
From Azure DDoS Protection metrics only
From Purview retention label analytics only
From Service Trust Portal audit PDFs only

explanation: Defender for Identity is built on Active Directory signals, typically collected with sensors in the AD environment. DDoS metrics, retention analytics, and STP PDFs are not that source.

stem: SOC analysts hunt across Defender XDR alerts in one operations console. A compliance officer needs Microsoft audit reports about Microsoft's own services. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Service Trust Portal is the XDR incident queue
Microsoft Defender portal for XDR operations; Service Trust Portal for Microsoft's audit and trust documents
The Defender portal publishes Microsoft's ISO audit PDFs as its primary job
Both jobs are done only in Azure Bastion

explanation: The Defender portal is for XDR operations. The Service Trust Portal publishes Microsoft's compliance evidence. They are frequently confused because both are 'portals'.

stem: Defender for Cloud can show regulatory-control status for Azure resources. Compliance Manager assesses the customer's implementation of compliance controls. Why switch products for those jobs?

choices.text: Compliance Manager remediates NSG rules as its primary job
Defender for Cloud is the only place to complete GDPR improvement actions for Microsoft 365
Azure/multicloud regulatory posture lives in Defender for Cloud; customer compliance assessments live in Purview Compliance Manager
They are the same score stored in Azure Bastion

explanation: A regulatory view of Azure resources is not the same as Compliance Manager's customer-control assessments. SC-900 expects that product split.
